set.summary: War between Israel and Hamas and other Gaza groups from 7 July 2014 (UN Commission of Inquiry dating; Israel dates Operation Protective Edge from 8 July) to 26 August 2014, 51 days counted from 7 July. Gaza groups fired 4,881 rockets and 1,753 mortars toward Israel; on 17 July Israel launched a ground operation that it said targeted cross-border tunnels, and the IDF found 32 tunnels, 14 of them extending into Israel. The UN Commission of Inquiry counted 2,251 Palestinians killed, including 1,462 civilians (551 children), and 11,231 injured; the IDF's preliminary analysis counted 2,125 dead, at least 936 of them militants and 761 civilians. At the height of hostilities about 500,000 people in Gaza (28% of the population) were displaced, and 18,000 housing units were destroyed or damaged (OCHA). 67 Israeli soldiers and 6 civilians in Israel were killed and up to 1,600 Israelis injured; according to sources cited by OCHA, as many as 70% of the roughly 40,000 residents of communities near Gaza left their homes. An Egyptian-brokered open-ended ceasefire began on 26 Aug 2014.

set.summary: Following weeks of tension and clashes in Jerusalem, Hamas and other Gaza groups fired rockets toward Jerusalem and central Israel from 10 May and Israel launched an 11-day air campaign. As of September 2021, OCHA, citing OHCHR, counted 261 Palestinians killed in Gaza, including 67 children (130 civilians, 64 members of armed groups, 67 undetermined), and over 2,210 injured; at the height of the escalation 113,000 Gazans were displaced. According to the same OCHA report, 13 people in Israel, including one soldier, were killed by Palestinian rocket fire. A ceasefire took effect on 21 May.

set.summary: From 8 October 2023 Hezbollah fired rockets, missiles and drones at northern Israel in support of Hamas and Israel struck back across south Lebanon, escalating to full-scale war in autumn 2024. Israel evacuated border communities, including Kiryat Shmona and Metula; in September 2024 the government said 68,000 northern residents remained displaced, at a cost of 8.64 billion shekels. In Lebanon, Israeli strikes had driven about 1.2 million people from their homes by the November 2024 ceasefire (AP), and Lebanon's health ministry counted at least 3,961 people killed and 16,520 injured between 8 October 2023 and 26 November 2024. By the ceasefire on 27 November 2024, more than 80 Israeli soldiers and 47 civilians in Israel had been killed, according to AP.

set.summary: Israel launched a surprise air campaign against Iran's nuclear programme, missile forces and military leadership on 13 June 2025; Iran answered with hundreds of ballistic missiles and drones. On 22 June US aircraft struck the Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan nuclear sites, and a US-brokered ceasefire took hold on 24 June. In Israel, 28 people were killed (Israeli medical officials) and 3,238 hospitalised (Health Ministry), and more than 9,000 were displaced from damaged homes, according to figures reported by the Times of Israel on 24 June 2025. As of 8 July 2025 Iran's government reported at least 1,060 killed (AP), while the US-based group HRANA counted 1,190 killed, including 436 civilians and 435 security force members.
